description: GitHub CLI: releases, workflow runs, merges, secrets, repository settings, gists, API writes, write commands, and read commands.

rules.note: A secret in a `gh` argument goes to GitHub.
A release change publishes or removes artifacts for users.
A change to repository secrets or variables changes what workflows get.
Deletion, archive, rename, transfer, or settings of a repository.
An API call with a method other than GET changes GitHub state.
A merge changes the base branch, usually a release branch such as `main`, and can start a deployment. A push to `main` has the same flag.
A workflow run or a workflow change can deploy or publish.

exemptions.note: GitHub Actions variables are plain configuration, not secrets. A change still gets the flag of `secret-or-variable-change`, and a secret value in an argument gets `secret-argument`.

safe.note: Reads of pull requests, issues, runs, repositories, workflows, releases, labels, and caches, and searches. Creation, comments, and other changes are writes (dev round 3).

writes.note: Commands that change GitHub state: new, changed, closed, or merged pull requests and issues, comments and reviews, new or forked repositories, labels, reruns and cancels of runs, and keys (policy v7). The base model gave `writes` 0.08 to `gh pr comment` on held-out v3.
`gh api` sends a POST request when the command has fields (`-f`, `-F`, `--input`) and no `GET` method. The analysis compares lowercase arguments, so `-f` also matches `-F`.
